values: 30-minute Rainbow class color sorting｜fully fictional

The 4-year-old paper goal is to put a red card into the red area, not a developmental standard. Ov1 four cards: A/B each record putting a red card into the red area 1 time; the C action observation is blank; D only records participating in the activity, with no sorting action. Tv1 is an idea for a large red flat picture card, with no real safety or approval evidence given.

Rv1 feedback log: A/B/C are logged as received, D is pending; receipt is not an action record, and participation is not completed sorting. Real times, prompts, implementation, effects, and approval are all not given; the codes do not refer to real children.

In the first 10 minutes rebuild the action and feedback four cards; in the middle 10 minutes compute the action record completeness rate and explain why D cannot be counted; in the last 10 minutes write the goal-preserving adjustment, verification roles, and communication draft. The A–D two-dimension comparison table, keeping Ov1/Rv1, C blank, D participation only, and the pending feedback.

2/4×100%=50% is only the prompt's specific sorting action record completeness rate. D participated but has no action record, so the numerator cannot become 3; it is not a children's mastery rate, accuracy rate, ability, or teaching effect.

subject.name: Preschool Teachers
subject.summary: Preschool teachers guide preschool children through play and activities to develop social, physical, and cognitive abilities according to a curriculum or lesson plan, observe learning, adjust teaching approaches, and communicate with families. O*NET 25-2011.00 and BLS 25-2011 are the same standalone occupation; special education teachers 25-2051 and center directors 11-9031 have separate duties and wages. Child safety, privacy, and teaching qualifications follow local requirements.
